title: Standing against all hatred
hookLine: every person is in the image of God
tomorrow: Owen and Yasmin both came to the cast party. what does each keep?

cards: Closing night. The cast bows, and backstage someone does an impression of the new girl's accent. People laugh.

It isn't about Jews this time. So is it still your fight? The Torah's answer starts on its first page, in the JPS 1917 translation: "And God created man in His own image, in the image of God created He him."

teach.b: Not one people, not one family: the first human, ancestor of everyone. The Mishnah asks why the Torah begins with a single person, and gives reasons.
One is for the sake of peace, so no one could ever say to another, my ancestor was greater than yours. Everyone shares the same one. Another is a picture.
A king stamps many coins with one seal, and they all come out alike. God stamped every human with the seal of the first, and not one comes out like another. One human family, and no copies.
In the Sifra, Rabbi Akiva calls love your neighbor as yourself a great principle of the Torah.

teach.h: THE BOOK OF THE GENERATIONS OF ADAM.
teach.b: Ben Azzai names a greater one: this is the book of the generations of Adam. Why greater? A neighbor can be narrowed to people like you.
Adam can't. So standing against all hatred is yesterday's lesson, widened.
A slur about someone's accent, skin, faith or body forgets the seal. Lived, it's the same calm skill: name it, stand beside the person, and don't wait until you're the target.
Something to tell a friend tonight: the Mishnah says humanity started with one person so nobody could brag about their ancestors.

how: Many Jewish communities teach that every person is created in God's image, b'tzelem Elohim, and join interfaith and neighborhood efforts against every kind of hatred, not only antisemitism.

games.q: what does “standing against all hatred” mean?
o: avoiding arguments by never talking about faith
refusing hatred toward anyone, since all bear God's image
defending only your own community when it's attacked

games.q: one human family — tap the pairs.
p: identical coins; God's makes none alike
the book of the generations of Adam

s: the Mishnah says humanity began with one person so no one could claim a greater ancestor
for the sake of peace: everyone shares the same first parent.
in the Mishnah's coin picture, God's stamp makes every person identical
a king's seal makes identical coins; God's seal makes every person different.
Ben Azzai held 'love your neighbor' to be the Torah's greatest principle
Akiva called it a great principle; Ben Azzai named 'the book of the generations of Adam' as greater.

games.q: your project partner keeps getting mocked for her religion, which isn't yours. what fits every image?
o: stand beside her and say plainly that it's not okay.
stay out of it; it's between her and her own community.
quietly suggest she keep her religion low-key at school.
games.why: every person bears the image, and everyone shares the first ancestor. standing up isn't only for your own group.

practice: Stand up, feet planted, the way you'd stand next to someone being mocked: not in front of them, beside them. Let your shoulders settle level, as if theirs were right there.
Hold it for a few breaths, and bring to mind one person who might need someone beside them this week.

wordCard.voice: Standing against all hatred: refusing to forget that every person carries the image of God, one human family with no copies.

orig.note: Hebrew: the image of God, in which Genesis says every human was made.

carryVoice: Keep it near: every image, every face, and one first ancestor for all of us. Two weeks, done.

sources.q: And God created man in His own image, in the image of God created He him

sources.ref: Mishnah Sanhedrin 4:5 (Adam created alone: for peace, that none say 'my father is greater than yours'; the king's seal and the coins)
Sifra, Kedoshim 4:12 (Akiva: love your neighbor is a great principle; Ben Azzai: 'this is the book of the generations of Adam', Genesis 5:1, is greater)
